resources.string: Find an unknown button
Find an unknown button

Some consoles have a button that no firmware uses. This looks for the chip pin it is wired to.\n\nFirst put the console down and don\'t touch anything for a few seconds. Then hold the unknown button until the result shows.
Start
Don\'t touch anything…
Hold the unknown button now and keep holding it. Starting in %1$d…
Keep holding the unknown button…
Scan again
This system can\'t read the chip pins yet: it needs a newer kernel.
The scan didn\'t finish. Try again.
The button is on %1$s.
The button is on %1$s, and that\'s %2$s. It works already.
The button is on %1$s. It\'s already added as an extra button; restart if it doesn\'t work yet.
The button is on %1$s, but the chip uses that pin for something else, so it can\'t be used as a button.
Several pins changed. Scan again and hold only the unknown button.
%1$s, that\'s %2$s
%1$s, used for something else
Nothing changed. Some buttons are wired to the power chip or not to the main chip at all; those can\'t be found this way.
No pin changed, but an ADC input moved.
ADC inputs that moved:
Channel %1$s: %2$d to %3$d
Channel %1$s: %2$d to %3$d (used by %4$s)
A button on an ADC input can\'t be used yet. Please send us a problem report so we can add it.
Use it as a button
Saving…
Restart to use it; it shows up as Extra button %1$d in Button mapping.
Saved, but Kernel Tweaks are switched off. Switch them back on in Settings > System > Kernel Tweaks and restart; it then shows up as Extra button %1$d in Button mapping.
Couldn\'t save it for the next start. Try again.
There are already 8 extra buttons, that\'s the most.
